name: Nikita Khrushchev
role: First Secretary of the CPSU (1953-1964) and Soviet premier (1958-1964)
summary: Khrushchev was a Marxist-Leninist who led the Soviet Union under single-party rule, a planned economy and collective farming. He denounced Stalin's cult of personality and mass repression in 1956, promoted peaceful coexistence and disarmament proposals, and also crushed the Hungarian uprising, ran an anti-religious campaign and kept Party control of press and arts.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Listed free medical services and social insurance among the state's provisions to citizens as achievements of Soviet socialism.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Argued repeatedly that the planned socialist system out-produces capitalism ('let's compete, who can produce the most goods for the people') and rested the Seven-Year Plan on state direction.

public-ownership.rationale: Defined communism as a society in which all means of production are public property and defended the state/collective ownership of Soviet industry and land.

property-fundamental.rationale: Said builders of communism must shed 'the habits of the private proprietor' and described factories and land as having been taken from capitalists and landowners.

cut-welfare.rationale: Presented state pensions, benefits, social insurance and free services as achievements and promised expansion in the Seven-Year Plan.

empower-police-military.rationale: Ordered large cuts in conventional forces and unilaterally demobilised 1,800,000 men, relying on missiles.

more-religion-public.rationale: Launched the 1958-64 anti-religious campaign that cut the number of open churches from about 22,000 to 7,873.

limit-growth.rationale: Made catching up with and passing US production the central goal of Soviet economic policy.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Highlighted Soviet use of atomic energy for peaceful purposes as an achievement and proposed European co-operation on it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Stated that wars of liberation are revolutionary wars, not only admissible but inevitable, and said socialist transition may be non-peaceful if exploiters use force.

central-planning.rationale: Presented and defended the Seven-Year Plan and Control Figures as proof that a planned socialist economy outpaces capitalism, and argued the point with Nixon.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Personally drove state-directed investment drives: the Virgin Lands campaign, the chemical industry programme and heavy targets for oil and power in the Seven-Year Plan.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Backed collective and state farming and discouraged private farming (e.g. taxes on livestock held privately) rather than spreading property among small owners.

one-party-rule.rationale: Defended the single-party system ('yes, there is actually one political party') and called the Communist Party the leading force of Soviet society.

political-violence-never.rationale: Stated that liberation wars are just, revolutionary and inevitable, and kept the possibility of non-peaceful transition to socialism.

war-builds-character.rationale: Said nuclear war has no winners ('a fool may start this war and a wise man won't be able to end it') and urged peace.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Said builders of communism must be free of selfishness and greed and of the habits of the private proprietor.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Stated that communism distributes 'to each according to his needs' and that the USSR was working toward it.

production-for-use.rationale: Said production under socialism serves the people's needs and that the Soviet Union needs no markets or profit-seeking, unlike 'multi-millionaires'.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Stated that under socialism products of labour are not 'appropriated by owners of enterprises' and that capitalists exploit and plunder working people.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Defended the dictatorship of the proletariat as a government of the working people that is firm against exploiters, and said organs of the state wither away only once communism's conditions exist.

collective-farming.rationale: Defended collective farms as socialist agriculture and pushed collective and state farm expansion, while seeking material incentives for collective farmers.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: At the 20th Congress and afterwards stated that war is 'not fatally inevitable', revising the older Leninist thesis, though he kept calling imperialism aggressive.

national-self-determination.rationale: Stated that Russian Communists have always championed the right of nations to self-determination and independent states.

class-collaboration.rationale: Said working people in capitalist countries are rightly struggling against those who exploit and plunder them.

dominated-front.rationale: Called for unity of the socialist states, the national liberation movement and the working class against imperialism.

workers-nation.rationale: Grounded policy in 'proletarian internationalism' and the unity of the international working class.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Named racial discrimination alongside imperialism and colonialism as a common hatred of nations.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Described the dictatorship of the proletariat as power over exploiters and bourgeois states as serving monopoly capital.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Reported Seven-Year Plan targets to more than double oil output (113 to 240 million tons) and promoted new oil and gas finds.

national-mission.rationale: Stated that the Soviet Union has never imposed its ideology on anyone nor intends to, least of all by force, expecting communism to win by example.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Revealed the NKVD's abuses, forced confessions and executions in the Secret Speech and supported rehabilitations, though limited prosecutions.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Said the Soviet Union built socialism alone and 'asking help from nobody' for a long period, and held it complete and lasting there.

population-transfer.rationale: Condemned the wartime deportation of whole nations (Karachai, Kalmyks, Chechens, Ingush, Balkars) as monstrous, not militarily justified and a violation of Leninist nationality policy.

vanguard-party.rationale: Wrote that the working class's decisive factor is political leadership by its vanguard Marxist-Leninist party.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Contested: said extreme methods were justified in Lenin's Civil War period but not after exploiting classes were liquidated, and denounced violations of legality under Stalin.

party-controls-media.rationale: Said the press is 'our chief ideological weapon' that must be in the hands of the most loyal people and defended Party guidance of literature and art.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Insisted writers who are Party members must keep their actions within Party discipline laid down in the Rules.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Defended Party guidance of art and attacked formalism and 'abstractionist rubbish', and denounced works at the 1962 Manege show, but also backed Solzhenitsyn's publication.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Proposed disbanding military blocs and offered to withdraw Soviet troops from Germany, Poland and Hungary if NATO withdrew, but kept the Warsaw Treaty meanwhile.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Expressed sympathy with the German desire to unite and said reunification should be reached by the two German states themselves, not by abolishing the GDR.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Said lack of taste and fads for formalism must be resolutely combated and denounced avant-garde art.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Wrote that political independence does not finally liberate former colonies; they must achieve economic independence and break foreign monopolies' hold, and urged a non-capitalist path.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Built and boasted of Soviet nuclear missiles ('we've beaten you in rockets'), relying on the Soviet arsenal not an ally's.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Rejected claims that the USSR is bureaucratic or not truly socialist, and stated that the USSR had built socialism and was building communism.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: His anti-religious campaign closed churches and banned children from services and outdoor worship.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Condemned raising one man into a superman with supernatural, god-like characteristics.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Condemned Stalin's arbitrariness and violation of Soviet laws and revolutionary legality.

leader-cult.rationale: In the Secret Speech condemned the cult of the individual around Stalin as alien to Marxism-Leninism.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: In the Secret Speech said the exploiting classes were already liquidated and socialist relations rooted when Stalin used mass repression; denied that class struggle continued in the USSR.

moral-incentives.rationale: Argued against Stalin-era neglect that 'you won't get far if the collective farmer has no material incentives', though also urged communist selflessness as an aim.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Condemned colonial rule as slavery and said colonial peoples have the right to break its chains.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Said imperialists keep colonies to accumulate more wealth by exploiting colonial and dependent peoples and that foreign monopolies keep former colonies down.

party-own-road.rationale: Said each country contributes its own form to socialism and the 20th Congress gave concrete form to different roads; also accepted Poland's new leadership and Yugoslavia's specific forms in 1956, but intervened in Hungary.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Promoted Soviet aid, credits and technical help to newly free countries as an 'internationalist duty', alongside their economic independence.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Contested: urged the Soviet Union to out-produce the US in consumer goods, while telling writers that Soviet workers act not for the 'golden calf' or personal enrichment.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Declared Soviet support for liberation wars and for peoples fighting for independence, including Algeria and Cuba.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Contested: sent troops to Hungary in 1956 after Nagy announced leaving the Warsaw Pact, but claimed the legitimate Hungarian government had asked for the help.

job-guarantee.rationale: Called the right to work, delivering people from the threat of unemployment, 'man's supreme right' and said the Soviet right to work is exercised in reality.

non-intervention.rationale: Contested: repeatedly pledged non-interference in internal affairs as a coexistence principle, yet intervened in Hungary and backed liberation wars.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Said the mass deportations of entire nations were not dictated by military considerations, rejecting the claim that those peoples were collectively disloyal.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Boasted of homes built and owned by collective farmers and intellectuals, alongside public ownership of the means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Rejected the question 'how can there be coexistence if you fight for communism' and insisted on peaceful coexistence and competition.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Contested: condemned Stalin's repression of Party dissenters, yet used troops in Hungary 1956 and crushed the Novocherkassk revolt in 1962.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Condemned imperialists for keeping colonies to extract wealth from colonial peoples.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Presented the Soviet plan for general and complete disarmament at the UN in 1959 and afterwards, including disbanding armies.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Denounced rule by arbitrary arrest and execution without trial and called for observance of legality and norms.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Led an anti-religious campaign including atheist propaganda; also defended the atheist Soviet government against Eisenhower's moral objections.

term-limits.rationale: Ordered a rule that a third of each Party committee's membership be replaced at every election, a form of mandatory turnover.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Gave up Soviet bases at Porkkala-Udd and Port Arthur and demanded that all foreign military bases be dismantled.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Stated the socialist principle that goods go to workers by quantity and quality of work, not to owners of enterprises.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Held that in Soviet society the working class has a government of its own and that socialism's political leadership belongs to the working class.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Stated the USSR renounces any policy leading to war and never imposes its ideology by arms, yet defended liberation wars and the Hungary intervention.

arms-reduction.rationale: Proposed general and complete disarmament and unilaterally cut Soviet forces by 1,800,000 men.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Said in 1956 that the working class could win a parliamentary majority and turn parliament into an instrument of the people's will, so the old state machinery need not be smashed.

farm-price-support.rationale: Raised state procurement prices and argued farmers need price levels and material inducements to produce; supported state purchase of collective farm output.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Pressed to ban nuclear weapons by agreement but kept and developed the Soviet arsenal while Western powers kept theirs.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Said the working people would never allow restoration of capitalism, return of factories to capitalists or of land to landowners, and denied that the USSR is a bureaucratic state.

notes: Born 15 April 1894, died 11 September 1971 (confirmed on Wikipedia). His memoirs (Khrushchev Remembers) and the 1961 Party Programme text could not be obtained as full text, so they were not used. Views on peaceful transition and war inevitability changed in 1956 (20th Congress).
